# Strong in the Broken Places
## Scripture
"But he said to me, 'My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.' Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me." – 2 Corinthians 12:9
## Reflection
Men are trained to hide weakness—to push through pain, mask the limp, and never let anyone see the crack in the armor. But Paul flips that instinct on its head. He doesn't just tolerate his weakness; he boasts in it. Why? Because weakness is where Christ's power shows up most clearly. A man who pretends he has it all together has no room for grace. A man who admits he doesn't—who brings his failures, his fears, and his fatigue into the light—invites the strength of God into the fight.

This isn't an excuse for laziness or sin. It's an invitation to honesty. The warrior who names his weakness is stronger than the one who hides it, because he's no longer fighting alone. Today, stop pretending. Bring your weakest place to God and let His power rest on you. That's not defeat—that's how real strength begins.
## Daily Challenge
Do a set of pushups to failure—then do five more. As you push through the last reps, thank God that His strength is made perfect when yours runs out.
